drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json, do-work/make_candidate_pool.py, read-data/template_blanks.py, do-work/render_choices_as_fills.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Pool.test_blanks_ranked_typed_chosen_and_rendered_as_fills)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Fill the blanks of my script template with sourced phrases a small model on my computer chooses, and leave a blank empty when no phrase has a source."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"<step>":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool row with tools:list {tool: "tool:fill-a-scripts-blanks-with-small-local-models"} and gets its run command and steps.

3. Your AI runs the steps in order on your computer, each as python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/{step}.py request.json: make_candidate_pool (phrases with a checkable source), rank_pool_for_blanks, make_typed_options, then one chooser (choose_fills_with_decider, judge_filled_lines_with_decider or choose_fills_with_language_model), then render_choices_as_fills.
4. Each step prints a last line {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2); the next step reads the previous step result as its input.

5. Tell the person which blanks were filled, with each value source, and which were left empty with what they need; a blank of type PERSON-LINE is never filled from a pool, and no value goes in without a source.

worked_examples.title: Two blanks of a made-up lamp-shop script filled, one left empty below the abstain line
worked_examples.ask: Fill the blanks of my lamp shop script from my listing, site and git history.
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Pool.test_blanks_ranked_typed_chosen_and_rendered_as_fills). The template is made from the made-up transcript "Today we open our new lamp shop with 40 lamps and a kind note" with blanks thing (FEATURE, matches "lamp shop") and count (NUMBER, matches "40"). The pool comes from listings/lamps.json, a site folder naming Brightlamp and a git repo with commits "Open the lamp shop" and "Add three lamps". choice.json = {"choices":{"thing":{"choice":"Lamp shop","confidence":0.9},"count":{"choice":"three lamps","confidence":0.4}}}; request.json for render_choices_as_fills = {"choice":"choice.json","options":<make_typed_options result>,"tag":"made-up","conf_key":"confidence","abstain":0.7,"template":<template>,"title":"chosen by {tag}"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: fills.thing = {"value":"Lamp shop","sources":["listings/lamps.json:1"],"note":"chosen by made-up"}; fills.count holds needs and no value, because its confidence 0.4 is below the abstain line 0.7; written.md is a file in the render folder and drift is measured against the template words.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read its fields and row type from your own store. Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the example rows to keep beside your own.
